title: Capability vectors, health provenance, and mesh-sync playbook
content:
Purpose
This note collects a pragmatic playbook for building the cluster inventory and service discovery layer we need for inference routing: a compact node capability vector, explicit provenance for health signals, and a mesh-sync reconciliation pattern for multi-region eventual-consistency. Goal is to end up with a small, stable API and a lightweight storage model that makes routing decisions deterministic and auditable.

Context and why this is different
We already have many ideas about node labels and heartbeat metrics. The gap we see in practice: (1) routing decisions depend on derived signals (e.g., 'can-serve-long-context'), but there is no agreed representation for how those derived signals were computed or last-validated, (2) cross-region control planes observe transient differences and we need a canonical way to declare which region is authoritative for which signal, and (3) the combination of capability labels and health scores should be a first-class, versioned object so rollbacks and incident postmortems can link routing anomalies to inventory changes.

Goals and constraints
- Small capability vector (<= 16 fields) per node that is cheap to replicate and expressive enough for routing heuristics.
- Every signal includes provenance: origin (agent/aggregator), sample_time, sample_window, and confidence_hint.
- Health scoring must be reproducible: provide a documented formula and keep the raw inputs.
- Multi-region mesh-sync uses CRDT-friendly writes with region ownership hints to avoid flip-flopping.
- Reconciler runs incremental, idempotent fixes and emits audit events for changes.
- Backwards compatibility: new derived signals are additive; older routers ignore unknown keys.

Proposed node capability vector (field list)
We recommend a compact flat map keyed by snake_case names. Each entry is a simple string/enum or small numeric value. Keep this separate from heavy telemetry. Example vector fields:
- node_id: unique node UUID
- infra_region: region code (e.g., us-west1)
- rack_zone: zone or rack identifier (short)
- gpu_family: enum (a100-80gb, a100-40gb, h100-80gb, t4, gtx)
- gpu_count: integer as string ("8")
- gpu_memory_gb: integer as string ("320")
- kernel_build: short string tag for driver/kernel ABI (e.g., k516-ubuntu22)
- supports_4k_context: true|false
- supports_bf16: true|false
- nvlink_topology: compact code (L1/L2/MESH/NONE)
- max_tokens_cached: integer as string
- preemptibility: none|spot|preemptible
- workload_tier: capacity|burst|gpu-pool-isolated
- reported_health_score: 0-100 (string)
- capability_version: semver string for vector schema

Note: raw telemetry (GPU temp, fan speed, memory usage) should not be duplicated into the vector; instead store raw time-series in TSDB and compute derived flags. The vector stores the last-computed derived flags and a pointer to provenance metadata.

Health signal provenance model
Every derived flag or health_score must include a provenance header with these fields: origin, computed_at, sample_window, aggregator_version, raw_ids (list of sample ids or pointers), and confidence_hint. We recommend storing provenance as a short opaque string token that references a separate provenance table in the inventory service (so vectors stay compact). Example provenance entry (conceptual):
- provenance_id: prov-2025-01-12-00043
- origin: node-agent-v2 or region-aggregator-v1
- computed_at: 2025-01-12T21:04:12Z
- sample_window: 60s
- aggregator_version: 1.3.2
- raw_ids: [tsdb:gpu-mem-12345, tsdb:gpu-temp-12346]  (stored as list in provenance store)
- notes: "derived health drop after driver upgrade; confidence low"

Signal scoring recipe (example)
To keep the implementation deterministic we publish the scoring recipe (reference implementation as a short script lives in the repo). Example formula (normalized 0-100):
- gpu_mem_headroom_pct * 0.4 + avg_gpu_load_ratio_negated * 0.35 + recent_hw_errors_penalty * -0.25 + (driver_mismatch ? -15 : 0)
Where: gpu_mem_headroom_pct = min(100, 100 * free_mem / total_mem)
avg_gpu_load_ratio_negated = 100 - avg_util_pct over 60s
recent_hw_errors_penalty = min(40, num_correctable_errors_last_10m * 5)
All intermediate values and raw inputs are stored in provenance so the exact health_score is reproducible.

Routing policy examples using capability vectors and provenance
1) Low-latency chat route: prefer nodes where workload_tier==capacity, preemptibility==none, reported_health_score >= 85, and supports_bf16==true. If no matches, fallback to burst pool but add inference-time token limit of 512.
2) Long-context generation: require supports_4k_context==true, gpu_memory_gb >= 160, nvlink_topology in {MESH,L1}, and reported_health_score >= 80. If provenance.confidence_hint == low, prefer nodes with more recent computed_at within the last 2 minutes.
3) Regional affinity: prefer nodes where infra_region matches request region; if health_score delta between local and remote > 20, use remote region only if latency penalty < 15ms.

Mesh-sync and control plane reconciliation pattern
We propose a pull-based mesh-sync combined with optimistic writes:
- Each region runs a local inventory writer that owns authoritative writes for nodes physically located in that region. Ownership is recorded as owner_region on vectors.
- Regions expose a compact change-log (append-only) per node_id containing vector updates and provenance_id. Entries are monotonic by sequence number.
- Mesh-sync jobs stream peer change-logs and apply updates locally only if incoming sequence is newer OR if incoming owner_region matches local node ownership (to allow cross-region takeover flows initiated by ops).
- Conflicts: if two regions publish different vectors with the same sequence number, we resolve by owner_region priority list (product-configured) and emit an audit event for manual reconciliation.
- Garbage collection: keep the last N vectors per node (N=50) and full provenance for N=10; older provenance is compacted into summary records.

APIs and storage suggestions
- Inventory API endpoints (REST):
  - GET /v1/nodes/:node_id/vector -> returns latest vector + provenance_id list
  - GET /v1/regions/:region/change-log?since_seq= -> compact append-only stream for mesh-sync
  - POST /v1/nodes/:node_id/provenance -> store provenance blob (auth ops/agent)
  - POST /v1/nodes/:node_id/vector -> write vector (requires agent credentials and owner_region header)
- Storage model: primary store = strongly-consistent small KV (Postgres with logical replication or CockroachDB); heavy telemetry = TSDB (Prometheus/Promscale). Change-log is an append-only table keyed by node_id + seq.

Operational playbook (reconciler and incident modes)
- Reconciler runs every 30s per region: consumes peers' change-logs, applies deterministic conflict-resolution, and emits audit events to Kafka.
- If reconciler detects flip-flop (same node toggling owner_region > 3 times in 5m), quarantine the node: mark workload_tier=quarantined and route only to isolated burst pool. Pager on threshold.
- Driver/firmware rollouts: when rolling drivers across a fleet, mark anticipated aggregator_version in change-log entries. Routers should temporarily lower routing weight for nodes with aggregator_version different from majority to avoid regression.

Example small audit event payload (single-line JSON string stored in events topic)
{"event":"vector_update","node_id":"node-1234","old_seq":42,"new_seq":43,"why":"health_drop_after_driver_upgrade","provenance":"prov-2025-01-12-00043"}

Backward compatibility and evolution strategy
- Capability vectors are versioned via capability_version. Routers must ignore unknown keys. We will maintain a schema registry documenting allowed keys per version.
- New derived flags must be gated behind a opt-in router flag for 4 weeks before being considered primary routing signals.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Should we allow region-level aggregators to inject derived signals that can override node-agent-derived ones, or should aggregator-derived signals be used only as advisory (lower precedence)? (ops/product tradeoff)
- How big should the provenance store be and what retention guarantees do we need for audits (90 days? 1 year?)
- Do we need signed provenance entries for private deployments (HSM/KMS signing)?

Next steps (tactical)
- Implement small PoC inventory writer that publishes vectors and provenance_id to local change-log (owner: Samir) 2wk spike.
- Add read-only mesh-sync consumer to staging that applies updates and exposes GET /v1/nodes/:node_id/vector (owner: Lena) 2wk spike.
- Draft a routing RFC showing how three canonical routes (low-latency chat, long-context, batch-embeddings) consume the vector + provenance (owner: Marcus) 1wk.
- Run a 1-day chaos test: force conflicting vector publishes from two regions and exercise reconciler resolution + alerting (owner: Priya) 1 day.

Appendix: tiny SQL sketch for change-log table
CREATE TABLE node_vectors (
  node_id text PRIMARY KEY,
  seq bigint NOT NULL,
  vector jsonb NOT NULL,
  provenance_id text,
  owner_region text NOT NULL,
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE node_vector_log (
  node_id text,
  seq bigint NOT NULL,
  vector jsonb NOT NULL,
  provenance_id text,
  owner_region text NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (node_id, seq)
);

Note: we store vector as jsonb in DB for flexibility but the API returns the compact flat map for routers. We will add a materialized view that flattens the common vector fields for fast reads.

Contacts and owners
- Priya Patel (doc owner, overall reconciliation testing)
- Samir Rao (inventory writer PoC)
- Lena Gomez (mesh-sync consumer and staging test)
- Marcus Liu (routing RFC)

Rough timeline
- PoC & mesh-sync consumer (6 weeks) -> internal trial in staging (2 weeks) -> limited rollouts to canary fleets (4 weeks) -> GA with observability + audit retention (Q2).

Notes to self / loose thoughts (scratchpad)
- Keep capability vector narrow: we tried to add too many boolean flags last time and it exploded cross-service compatibility.
- Provenance tokens should be small (prov-YYYYMMDD-####) to make logs readable.
- Consider small SDK helper to fetch both vector and provenance in one RPC for routers to avoid two round trips.

End of doc.
